title: Review of c10's membrane_evo disk-births finding: on fresh seeds 21 and 22, 78% of births have a disk-cut parent (93% of K2 births) and 78% of deaths are disk erasures; with p_death=0 there is no reproduction (Supported)
summary: Looked at summary.txt and selection_c10.png, then ran c10's evotrack_disk.py on fresh seeds 21 and 22 for the up arm (b2=0.0845) and the identical-event twin (T=40000). Births whose parent a death disk overlapped in the same census: up 29/37 and 33/48, twin 36/44 and 33/38, in total 131/167 (78%; c10: 85%); K2 births 28/30 disk-cut (93%; c10: 95%); deaths that are disk erasures 98/126 (78%; c10: 85%) (data/summary.txt). The labkit re-runs of the up arm on these seeds (rerun_up/seed21, seed22; from my review 20261025T0746-c03-review-membrane-evo) show the disk cuts and regrowing fragments. My p_death=0 runs there gave 0-1 persistent splits per run, matching c10's 0-7 births without disks. The fractions are a little lower than c10's, but the reading holds: reproduction in membrane_evo runs on imposed fragmentation.

observations.D: data/summary.txt: 131/167 births disk-cut, 28/30 K2 births disk-cut on fresh seeds 21-22; rerun_up/seed21/sheet.png disk cuts (black disks) followed by regrowing fragments

controls_run.D: identical-event twin arm (data/tw_s21.log, tw_s22.log) and the p_death=0 runs of research/alife/collective/contrib/20261025T0746-c03-review-membrane-evo (ctl_*_nodeath: 0-1 persistent splits)

verdicts.limitation: The tracker credits a birth to a disk when any disk overlapped the parent in the same 100-step census, so some births near but not caused by a cut are counted; the fraction is 69-87% per run rather than c10's 83-85%.
